publications.title: A Deep Learning Based Framework for Solar Panel Segmentation and Fault Classification Enhanced with Explainable AI
publications.abstract: With the increasing adoption of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems worldwide, efficient monitoring and fault detection have become essential to ensure optimal performance and longevity. Traditional PV panel inspection methods are often time-consuming, labor-intensive, and lack precision. To address these challenges, this study presents a deep learning-based framework for solar panel segmentation along with fault and abnormality classification enhanced with LIME-based Explainable AI (XAI). The proposed approach employs a hybrid segmentation model that combines the strengths of U-Net and RefineNet, leveraging DenseNet as the backbone. The segmentation module performs binary segmentation to ensure precise localization of solar panels before the fault classification stage. For fault classification, a MobileNetV3Small-based transfer-learning model is utilized, which can classify diverse real-world fault and abnormality conditions, including physical and electrical damage, dust, bird droppings, and snow cover. LIME-based XAI is incorporated to improve interpretability, providing insight into the model's decision-making. The segmentation model achieved an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 93.63% and 91.24% on two publicly available datasets, and the classification model attained 97.53% accuracy. The proposed method outperforms existing approaches in both segmentation and classification while maintaining computational efficiency, enabling automated solar panel monitoring with high reliability and transparency.
highlights: Two-stage pipeline: pixel-wise semantic segmentation first isolates individual PV modules, then a downstream classifier assigns module-level fault categories — decoupling localization from diagnosis.
Explainable-AI attribution maps expose the visual evidence behind each fault prediction, making the model auditable for field operations & maintenance rather than a black box.
Handles real-world PV inspection imagery, addressing class imbalance across rare fault types and domain variability in illumination and panel condition.
Published in Solar Energy (Elsevier, IF 6.6), a leading venue for photovoltaic and solar-systems research.

publications.title: MonoSIM: An Open-Source SIL Framework for Ackermann Vehicular Systems with Monocular Vision
publications.venue: IEEE 12th Intl. Conf. on Automation, Robotics and Applications (ICARA)
publications.abstract: This paper presents an open-source Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) simulation platform designed for autonomous Ackermann vehicle research and education. The proposed framework focuses on simplicity while making it easy to work with small-scale experimental setups such as the XTENTH-CAR platform. The system was designed using open-source tools, creating an environment with a monocular camera vision system to capture stimuli with minimal computational overhead through a sliding-window based lane detection method. The platform supports a flexible algorithm testing and validation environment, allowing researchers to implement and compare various control strategies within an easy-to-use virtual environment. To validate the platform, Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) algorithms were implemented within the SIL framework. The results confirm that the platform provides a reliable environment for algorithm verification, making it an ideal tool for future multi-agent system research, educational purposes, and low-cost AGV development. Code: https://github.com/shantanu404/monosim.git
highlights: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) framework that closes the perception-to-control loop for Ackermann-steered vehicles entirely in simulation, removing hardware from early-stage algorithm validation.
Uses a single monocular camera as the sole exteroceptive sensor, tackling scale-ambiguous perception without LiDAR or stereo depth.
Explicitly models Ackermann steering kinematics so control and path-tracking behaviour transfers meaningfully toward real platforms.
Released open-source for reproducibility; developed from the author's undergraduate thesis.

publications.title: A Robust Deep Learning Framework for Bangla License Plate Recognition Using YOLO and Vision-Language OCR
publications.venue: IEEE Intl. Conf. on AI and Data Analytics (ICAD)
publications.abstract: An Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) system constitutes a crucial element in an intelligent traffic management system. However, the detection of Bangla license plates remains challenging because of the complicated character scheme and uneven layouts. This paper presents a robust Bangla License Plate Recognition system that integrates a deep learning-based object detection model for license plate localization with Optical Character Recognition for text extraction. Multiple object detection architectures, including U-Net and several YOLO (You Only Look Once) variants, are compared for license plate localization. This study proposes a novel two-stage adaptive training strategy built upon the YOLOv8 architecture to improve localization performance. The proposed approach outperforms established models, achieving an accuracy of 97.83% and an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 91.3%. The text recognition problem is phrased as a sequence generation problem with a VisionEncoderDecoder architecture, and a combination of encoder-decoders is evaluated. The ViT + BanglaBERT model gives the best results at the character level, with a Character Error Rate of 0.1323 and Word Error Rate of 0.1068. The system also shows consistent performance on an external dataset curated for this study, offering completely different environment and lighting conditions from the training sample, indicating the robustness of the framework. Overall, the proposed system provides a robust and reliable solution for Bangla license plate recognition and performs effectively across diverse real-world scenarios, making it well suited for deployment in intelligent transportation applications such as automated law enforcement and access control.
highlights: Cascades a YOLO detector for plate localization with a vision-language OCR stage for reading, separating 'where' from 'what' for robustness.
Targets Bangla script — conjunct characters, non-Latin glyphs and compact multi-line layouts that break conventional OCR engines.
Leverages a vision-language model for recognition, moving beyond fixed-character-set classifiers toward context-aware transcription.
Emphasizes robustness under real traffic conditions: varied fonts, viewing angles, resolution and lighting.

publications.title: Long-Term Energy Demand Analysis Using Machine Learning Algorithms: A Case Study in Bangladesh
publications.abstract: In every energy sector, from production to consumption, machine learning and statistical models have influenced the power system for the past few decades. Among these, energy demand analysis is an important research area in Bangladesh due to its necessity. This study introduces energy consumption forecasting along with the necessary environmental feature variables. Energy demand varies depending on short-term, medium-term, and long-term analysis; this paper focuses on long-term energy demand while predicting energy consumption. The dataset includes three years of monthly data comprising more than one million samples and diverse consumer types, with versatile features from the capital of Bangladesh, Dhaka (mainly Uttara). Different machine learning models — Random Forest, k-nearest Neighbors regression, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting (LightGBM) — were used, and various performance metrics were applied to evaluate them. Among the models, KNN performed considerably well, with an R-squared of about 0.9447, RMSE of 163.9, and MAE of 28.7. Such a study will help upgrade the power system management of Bangladesh.
highlights: Comparative study of multiple machine-learning regressors for long-horizon electricity-demand forecasting on Bangladesh national data.
Feature engineering over socio-economic and temporal demand drivers to capture long-term growth trends.
Benchmarks model families to surface accuracy/robustness trade-offs relevant to energy-planning decisions.
Framed as a policy-relevant case study for a fast-growing developing-country grid.

publications.title: Optimizing Master-Slave Broadcast Communication in Multi-Node Network Using RS485 Standard
publications.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the implementation of master-slave broadcast communication over a differential signalling standard (RS-485) that defines the electrical interface and physical layer for connecting electrical devices. The focus is on the design and timing analysis of a communication system involving multiple STM32 microcontrollers arranged in a daisy-chain configuration. The master device broadcasts commands to multiple slave devices, which, after receiving the commands, send feedback to the master as well as to other slaves. The system uses Direct Memory Access (DMA) for efficient data transfer, Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) for error detection, and precise timing control to ensure reliable communication. A key feature is its unique feedback mechanism, where all nodes receive data and execute commands, but only the addressed node provides feedback. Multiple nodes then accept this feedback, ensuring synchronized operation and real-time updates across the network. The system has been rigorously tested on a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) with a 6-degree-of-freedom (DOF) arm and differential drive, demonstrating its reliability and efficiency in controlling complex robotic movements and feedback mechanisms.
highlights: Designs and optimizes a master–slave communication scheme over UART/RS485 across multiple STM32 microcontroller nodes.
Contrasts broadcast versus unicast messaging patterns and their impact on bus utilization and latency.
Addresses half-duplex RS485 bus arbitration and node addressing for reliable multi-node embedded networking.
A practical embedded-systems contribution for distributed sensor and actuator networks.

projects.title: Man-Transportable EOD ROV (JS2.0)
projects.subtitle: A single-soldier-deployable Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) robot with a 7-DOF arm.
projects.description: A compact, man-transportable EOD ROV with a tracked base, telescopic 7-DOF arm and integrated disrupter, built on lessons from the medium-platform Jontro Soinik.
projects.specsFile: data/Projects/Manportable EOD JS2.0/Electrical and Mechanical Specs.md
contribution: Primary developer of a real-time, safety-critical **EOD robot** — tracked base, 7-DOF arm, integrated disrupter, and a redundant wired/wireless control link — implementing most of the system across the **full stack from embedded firmware to operator HMI**.

Developed a **custom CANopen (CiA-402) control library** driving **11 servo drives on two 1 Mbit/s CAN buses** in position, velocity and torque modes — cyclic SDO setpoints at 50 Hz with interrupt-driven TPDO telemetry, plus differential-joint, lead-screw and worm-gear drivetrain modeling.

Wrote **STM32F103 firmware** that transparently tunnels the SBUS RC stream over a WIZnet-W5500 UDP link (UART-DMA idle-line framing, interrupt-driven sockets, PHY-loss recovery) with automatic **hardware failover to a wireless backup** on wired-link loss.

Derived and shipped a **closed-form inverse-kinematics solver** for the telescoping 7-DOF arm, verified against the URDF and integrated with **MoveIt 2** for collision-validity checks and home-pose planning.

Engineered a **layered fail-safe system** for a weaponized platform: asymmetric per-bus fault isolation with full-disarm, latched safe states, a degraded loopback mode, an encoder-battery startup gate, and fail-safe disrupter fire-control that disarms the instant the operator link drops.

Built the **operator console** (Android/Kotlin): 5-feed low-latency RTSP switching (hardware MediaCodec), a real-time telemetry dashboard (Jetpack Compose), a **3D digital-twin OpenGL overlay**, two-way echo-cancelled intercom, gimbal control and the fire-control UI.

projects.title: Autonomous Guided Vehicle (AGV) — CYBERFLEET
projects.subtitle: An autonomous 3-robot warehouse AGV fleet built on ROS 2.
contribution: Architected and built an end-to-end **ROS 2 (rclpy)** autonomy platform for a 3-robot AGV fleet delivering goods between warehouse stations — spanning perception, localization, planning, control, actuation, safety and fleet orchestration.

Developed a **5-state EKF** (`x, y, theta` + linear/angular velocity biases) fusing wheel odometry (predict @ 50 Hz) with absolute **AprilTag 36h11** camera observations; implemented **Joseph-form** covariance updates and **OOSM rewind/replay** to correctly fuse latency-delayed measurements.

Built the **AprilTag localization front end** — OpenCV calibration/undistortion, planar tag-pose estimation, multi-gate outlier rejection, and a surveyed 120-tag world map with per-tag orientation resolution.

Implemented **space-time A-star** path planning over a discretized 63x171 grid with headings and per-move timing; added a peer **reservation table** with head-on swap detection and a turn-minimizing cost model.

Wrote the **plan-manager orchestrator** (async non-blocking planning, exponential replan backoff, obstacle-triggered replanning) plus a 50 Hz **feedforward + PD trajectory-tracking controller** with cubic-Bezier interpolation and differential-drive mixing.

Engineered **FleetCore**, the central coordinator: 3 concurrent per-robot FSMs (~20 states), FIFO dispatch, atomic **lift/scanner mutual exclusion** with staging queues, and publish-until-accept command delivery.

blog.title: STM32 Ethernet Communication Tutorial using WIZnet W5500 Module
blog.excerpt: A comprehensive guide on Ethernet communication using the WIZnet W5500 module. We demonstrate how to use the W5500 IC to send messages to a computer as well as receive messages from it, building an example project on the popular STM32 "Blue Pill" (STM32F103C8T6) board.

blog.title: Ethernet Communication using STM32 Microcontroller and WIZnet (Interrupt Mode)
blog.excerpt: The WIZnet module is a compact Ethernet networking module based on WIZnet's W5x00 series chips (e.g. W5500), providing a hardwired TCP/IP stack for easy integration with microcontrollers via SPI. It enables stable, low-resource Ethernet with support for multiple sockets — ideal for IoT and embedded systems needing reliable wired networking.
